audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Cass/Cass/Cass/Skill/Cass/Skill/Cass. It disagreed with the packet chart on three rows and, worse, with its own text: whys[3] says Miasma keeps you unable to close at 4-5, whys[5] says her first AP item keeps her ahead, and whys[6] plus spikes[3] and late all say Yasuo finally wins late — yet the chart gave the late row to Cassiopeia.
audit.why: Miasma grounds Yasuo's E for its whole duration on a 24s rank-1 cooldown, so every lane phase is hers; only full crit plus a wall that eats Twin Fang flips the 2-item duel.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 through First item read Cassiopeia; 2+ items reads Yasuo. Matches the packet chart. Rows proposed as a matched full+content group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why and phases[5].why were generic template lines ('the lane-control window', 'Blade of the Ruined King is your spike') that credited Yasuo with windows the rest of the page gives to Cassiopeia, and neither carried a cooldown number.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 — a long, countable window, and the gap after it expires is Yasuo's only clean E-Q. Her first AP item out-damages his first item because Twin Fang chains at 0.75s while he is grounded.
audit.corrected: phases[3].why now gives Miasma's 24s and the post-expiry window; phases[5].why states why her item beats his.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places told the player Wind Wall stops Noxious Blast and Petrifying Gaze: spikes[3] 'you can wall her Q and R', late 'wall her Q and R', wants.you[1] 'wall her Q and R', whys[6] 'wall her R'. dosFull[2].t said 'Windwall his Miasma'.
audit.why: Noxious Blast is a delayed ground zone and Miasma is a set of clouds — neither is a projectile, and Riot's text for Petrifying Gaze describes a cone of energy from her eyes with no projectile flag. The one thing in her kit the wall does eat is Twin Fang, which is flagged projectile and is her entire sustained damage. spikes[0] already had this right; the rest of the page contradicted it.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall is now stated as the answer to Twin Fang everywhere, and the false Q/R claims are gone. Petrifying Gaze handled by facing away, which turns the stun into a slow. Added Twin Fang's healing and the Executioner's Calling answer.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Miasma's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Miasma is 24s at rank 1 and grounds your E for its whole duration. Farm safe, and only step up in the window after it expires.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Miasma's cooldown.
edits.after: Her first AP item out-damages your first: Twin Fang chains through you while Miasma holds you in place.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Twin Fang heals her off every tick — Executioner's Calling is core.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze (R) stuns you if you're facing her — a free full combo. Turn your back to break line of sight or eat the stun and die. Her W grounding plus R makes this her strongest all-in window; play back and don't give her the frontal engage.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze (R) stuns you if you're facing her — a free full combo. Turn your back — facing away turns the stun into a slow. Her W grounding plus R makes this her strongest all-in window; play back and don't give her the frontal engage.

edits.before: Yasuo finally wins late: with full crit and Wind Wall you can wall her Q and R, and if you catch her without Miasma up your E-Q burst ends her squishy frame. Bait her W grounding, turn to avoid the R stun, and gap-close the instant the pool is down.
edits.after: Yasuo finally wins late: with full crit and a wall that eats Twin Fang, if you catch her without Miasma up your E-Q burst ends her squishy frame. Bait her W grounding, turn to avoid the R stun, and gap-close the instant the pool is down.

notes: The mirror audit's Medium-confidence read that Petrifying Gaze passes Wind Wall matches what I found: no projectile flag and Riot's text describes a cone from her eyes. I did not write that the wall blocks it and I did not write that it cannot — I replaced the claim with the facing mechanic, which is in Riot's text. The page also calls Cassiopeia 'he' throughout the full layer's boilerplate; flagged for a champion-level pronoun sweep, not hand-edited.
